title: Deploying to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages

videos.script:
This course starts at the push. You have an app, and you have a repository. Now somebody else has to be able to open it.

{{files}} The first thing to see is that a built front end is a folder of files. An HTML page, a script, a stylesheet, some data. Nothing in it runs on a server. Deploying it means putting those files somewhere that answers requests for them.

{{planner}} The app for the whole course is a study planner. It lists courses, opens one, adds sessions and totals the week. You build it in this lesson, in plain TypeScript with Vite, so no framework is assumed.

{{host}} Then you serve the built folder the way a static host does, on your own computer, with a server of about forty lines that you can read. Every host in this lesson does what it does, plus a network of copies around the world.

{{four}} Then the four hosts. Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages. What each one asks you for, and where each one differs. None of them is run here, and the lesson says so each time.

{{subpath}} And the one difference that breaks sites on the first day: a site served from a folder, not from the root of a domain.
